# About this book {.unnumbered #sec-about}

LightHit computes the light seen by a point detector in a scattering medium
without simulating individual photon histories. A photon emitted in water
either reaches the detector directly, changes direction after one or more
scattering events, or is absorbed. Rather than sampling this random walk,
the package solves for the photon distribution directly and evaluates the
part of it that a given detector would register.

This book documents the first module of that package: the Green's function
of a point source and a point isotropic detector in an infinite, homogeneous
medium with Henyey–Greenstein scattering. @sec-rte derives the radiative
transfer equation (RTE) that the whole package solves, starting from a
photon balance and fixing the notation used throughout. @sec-point-source
solves it for a point source and a point detector: an adjoint formulation
turns the angular problem into a finite linear system with an exact free
tail, and the result decomposes into three parts — no scattering, exactly
one scattering, and two or more. @sec-histogram-binning explains why the
first two parts are computed differently from the third: they are singular
in physical time, and folding a finite time bin onto them analytically
avoids a numerically dangerous Fourier inversion. @sec-bgvd-water applies
the solver to the measured optical properties of Lake Baikal water at one
wavelength.

Our worked example is Cherenkov light propagating to the optical modules of
a neutrino telescope. Nothing here yet needs a shower model, a Geant4 event
format, or detector electronics; those attach to a transport model that is
already understood on its own, not alongside it.

Familiarity with derivatives, multivariate integrals, linear algebra, and
elementary probability is assumed. Spherical-harmonic and operator notation
is introduced where it is first needed. The reference implementation is in
`src/lighthit`; equations here are cross-referenced to the functions that
implement them.

## What "solution" means here {.unnumbered}

The book distinguishes an exact solution of the original RTE, an exact
solution of an approximated equation, and a numerical estimate of one
observable. A finite-rank truncation of the scattering operator at degree
$L$ is an approximation of the RTE; the linear system built from that
truncation is then solved exactly. "All orders of scattering" is likewise
scoped to that same finite-rank approximation: increasing the number of
retained angular moments and increasing the number of scattering events
summed are different knobs, and both are reported separately wherever they
matter.

## Status {.unnumbered}

This is the first module: a point source, a point isotropic detector, one
wavelength at a time, an infinite homogeneous medium. A finite optical
module, real detector acceptance, shower sources, and a spatial cache for
reusing computations across many source–detector pairs are future work,
tracked in `STATE.md` at the repository root.

The radiative transfer equation and its photon-balance derivation in
@sec-rte follow the treatment in the author's own lecture notes on radiative
transfer for the Baikal-GVD programme; the material is rewritten here for
this package, not reproduced verbatim, and is scoped to what @sec-point-source
and @sec-histogram-binning actually use.
